newsitem.title: USA: CBOT wheat closes nearly flat on late local sales.
newsitem.headline: CBOT wheat closes nearly flat on late local sales.

text.p: Late local selling took the bloom from a mild low volume rally and CBOT wheat futures sagged from the day's highs near the close but ended nearly unchanged, traders said.
"It was all local selling, there was nothing else in here," a trader said.
The market was firm early on several fundamental factors including export news and on news the European Union (EU) had slowed down its wheat export pace.
"Export sales were good," said Vic Lespinasse of Dean Witter Reynolds.
USDA early Friday said U.S. net export sales of wheat during the week ended January 16 totaled 590,900 tonnes, above expectations for 250,000 to 300,000 tonnes.
Short covering after the declines in wheat Wednesday and again Thursday contributed to the advances in wheat futures early in the session.
Wheat closed 1/2 cent per bushel higher to 3/4 lower, with March down 3/4 at $3.75. July ended up 1/2 at $3.44-1/4.
But the brighter export hopes were central to the gains early in the session.

Paris-based traders and officials late this week said the EU all but slammed the door on grains exports on Thursday in a surprise move that owed as much to swirling currency movements as the fragile state of world prices.

Gains were limited by further indications India may not be in the market for any more wheat. Traders and analysts in New Delhi Friday said a drop in domestic wheat prices and hopes of a good crop might prompt India to buy less than the two million tonnes of wheat it planned to import by March.
Commercial and speculative positioning was light and on each side of the market in quiet dealings.
Wheat futures volume was estimated at 11,000 contracts, below the 14,787 traded Thursday.
In wheat options, FIMAT Futures bought 200 March $3.90 calls and bought 200 March $3.90 puts at 19 cents, traders said.
Wheat options volume was estimated at 3,500 contracts, below the 5,073 traded Thursday.
